## Part 2 — Why This Is Critical (Data-Backed)

Pulling from research:

> "**Facebook isn't primarily where patients discover your practice from scratch. It's where they go to verify that you're real, active, and trustworthy before they call. A profile with no posts, outdated information, or a missing cover photo sends a message. That message is not a good one.**" — Arcane Marketing, 2026

> "**76% of consumers who see a local dental ad on Facebook visit the practice within a month.**" — WorldMetrics 2026

> "**97% of dentists use Facebook as their main social media page.**" — Arch Dental Marketing 2026

> "**5-star reviews on Google increase a dental practice's visibility by 48% in local search results.**" — WorldMetrics 2026 (this is Google reviews, but FB reviews have a parallel effect on FB-local search)

> "**Social media engagement for dental practices is 2.3x higher than the national average for small businesses.**" — WorldMetrics 2026 (so the ceiling is HIGHER than for, say, a coffee shop)

> "**Best practices:**
> - 3-4 posts/week minimum for healthcare pages
> - Patient testimonials drive 5x more conversions than text-only
> - Consistent NAP (Name/Address/Phone) across all platforms is a local SEO signal
> - Cover photo is the most valuable visual real estate
> - Reviews tab must be enabled + actively seeded" — Arcane + RevenueWell + Sendible

### Local SEO ranking signals that depend on this FB page

1. **NAP consistency** (name, address, phone across web) — FB page is one of the top 5 citation sources Google uses
2. **Page activity** — active pages rank higher in "near me" searches
3. **Reviews on the platform** — FB Reviews count toward Google's local pack ranking
4. **Backlinks** — FB page is a citation that supports your domain authority
5. **Click-through signals** — branded searches that include "facebook.com" pass trust

**A dormant FB page hurts your Google ranking too.** This isn't just a social media problem — it's an SEO problem.

## Part 7 — Long-Term Strategic Recommendations

### What most dentists get wrong on Facebook

1. **Posting without a strategy.** Random posts = random engagement = zero compounding. Stick to the content pillars (4 of them): educational (40%), trust-building (30%), promotional (20%), community (10%).

2. **Treating it as a billboard.** FB rewards conversation, not broadcast. Every post should invite a response.

3. **Ignoring DMs.** A DM unanswered for 2 hours = patient goes to the next dentist. Set up auto-reply + a human responder.

4. **Not collecting reviews.** Reviews are the #1 conversion driver on local business pages. A page with 50 5-star reviews converts 5-10x better than one with 0.

5. **Posting and ghosting.** The "post and pray" approach. Engagement compounds: respond to every comment within 4 hours.

### The compounding effect of a well-maintained page

If you do this right:
- **Month 1:** 0 → 100 followers, 3 reviews, 20+ posts
- **Month 3:** 500 followers, 15 reviews, 100+ posts, 8 bookings from FB
- **Month 6:** 1,000+ followers, 30+ reviews, 250+ posts, 30+ bookings from FB, $200+/month ad spend justified
- **Year 1:** 2,000+ followers, 100+ reviews, dominant local search presence for "dentist Asunción," 100+ bookings/year from FB

The compounding only works if you START. Right now we're at 0 — there's nowhere to go but up.

### The patient journey you'll be enabling

1. Patient Googles "dentista bilingüe Asunción"
2. Sees your Google Business Profile with photos + reviews
3. Sees your website (already optimized)
4. Searches "Ometz Dental Facebook" — finds a professional, active page with 50 reviews + 100 posts
5. Clicks WhatsApp CTA → messages you → you book them
6. They come in, get great treatment
7. They leave a review + refer a friend
8. Loop continues

Every link in that chain matters. Right now link #4 is the weakest.
